newsitem.title: USA: High school player slashes opponents with buckles.
newsitem.headline: High school player slashes opponents with buckles.

text.p: A New Mexico high school football player faces a criminal investigation for slashing members of an opposing team with razor-sharp buckles on his helmet, officials said on Tuesday.

Mike Cito was expelled from St Pius X High School on Monday after using the sharpened chin-strap buckles to injure four Albuquerque Academy players in a game 10 days ago. One player needed 10 stitches to a cut on his forearm.
Cito's father, Stephen Cito, admitted filing the metal buckles to a fine edge. He said he did it to get even with players who roughed up his son in previous games.
District Attorney Bob Schwartz said other players on Cito's team may also have deliberately slashed opposing players.
"We'll have to see what adults are involved in this because I don't think it ends with the kids," said Schwartz.
